name: Silk weaving in Yangshao-culture Henan
summary: Researchers found carbonised silk fabric in a Yangshao-period urn burial at Wanggou, Henan, reported at about 5,500 to 5,300 years old.
description: The China National Silk Museum reported two textile structures in carbonised material from Wanggou urn W12. A finer crossed-warp fabric was identified as silk by an immunoassay. The team tentatively interpreted the structure as leno weave. The find documents a woven silk textile in a burial.

impact.note: Scores reflect the general importance of silk manufacture. The Wanggou burial documents woven silk locally.

date.label: c. 3550 to 3350 BCE (5,500 to 5,300 years ago)
date.basis: Approximate age range reported in the 2019 Xinhua account. The museum’s W12 laboratory note identifies the fabric and does not give a direct date.

events.statement: The China National Silk Museum identified carbonised crossed-warp fabric from urn W12 at Wanggou as silk.

evidence.locator: pp. 44–45 (PDF p. 32), testing of residues from the Wanggou urn burials
evidence.supports: Reports plain-weave and finer crossed-warp material in W12 and identifies the crossed-warp fabric as silk with ELISA.
The silk fabrics at the Wanggou date back between 5,300 and 5,500 years.
evidence.locator: Paragraph on dating, after the ELISA identification

events.caveats: The W12 test identifies silk in the crossed-warp material. The age in the press account is contextual. The specimen establishes cloth in the burial; the place of its manufacture and the way the silk was obtained remain open.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated Wanggou burial is the contextual witness to woven silk in this record.

unresolved.note: Find the W12 excavation and dating report to establish the sampling context and calibrated age for this specific deposit.
Seek a local loom-associated assemblage or cocoon evidence contemporaneous with the tested fabric. The Shuanghuaishu carving is an animal depiction and does not establish domestication.
Jiahu soil peptides are a different kind of evidence. There is no demonstrated transmission to Wanggou or to the later Qianshanyang material.

research.note: The China National Silk Museum laboratory report supplies the W12 specimen identification. Xinhua reports the team's contextual dating and does not independently confirm the assay. Directly dated silk cloth, silkworm domestication and yarn preparation remain separate questions.
